nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Light drives the dune plants and the plankton in the cold coastal water.

nodes.name: Cold nutrient-rich water
nodes.desc: Cool, nutrient-bearing Atlantic water feeds plankton, and plankton feed the fish that the seals depend on.

nodes.name: Moving sand dunes
nodes.desc: Wind-shifted dunes up to about 30 m high hold salt-tolerant, sand-adapted plants that anchor the sand.

nodes.name: Dune insects & bacteria
nodes.desc: Carcass-feeding insects and microbes break down dead matter along the shore and return nutrients to the sand.

nodes.name: Phytoplankton
nodes.desc: Microscopic algae in the offshore waters that start the marine food chain.

nodes.name: Dune grasses
nodes.desc: Grasses and other low herbs of the stabilised dunes and coastal grassland, eaten by burrowing and grazing rodents.

nodes.name: Sea rocket
nodes.desc: A salt-tolerant pioneer plant of beaches and foredunes, recorded near Cabo Polonio.

nodes.name: Hedge cactus
nodes.desc: A tall cactus of the coastal scrub whose fruit is eaten by birds and lizards.

nodes.name: Zooplankton
nodes.desc: Drifting animals that graze phytoplankton and feed small fish.

nodes.name: Argentine anchoita
nodes.desc: A small schooling fish feeding on plankton. Anchovies are a main prey of Uruguayan fur seals.

nodes.name: Pearson's tuco-tuco
nodes.desc: A burrowing rodent and the dominant vertebrate of the Cabo Polonio dunes.

nodes.name: Brazilian guinea pig
nodes.desc: A wild cavy that grazes grass and herbs in coastal scrub and is prey for foxes, tegus and small cats.

nodes.name: Rufous-collared sparrow
nodes.desc: A very common small bird that eats seeds, insects and fruit, including hedge cactus fruit.

nodes.name: South American fur seal
nodes.desc: Breeds on the Islas de Torres. Eats fish such as anchovies and squid, and is hunted by sharks, orcas and sea lions.

nodes.name: Franciscana
nodes.desc: A small coastal dolphin, the best-recorded mammal here, that feeds on fish and squid in shallow water.

nodes.name: Kelp gull
nodes.desc: Nests on the offshore islands and feeds on fish, invertebrates and scavenged food.

nodes.name: Argentine tegu
nodes.desc: A large omnivorous lizard that eats fruit, small mammals and other prey.

nodes.name: Pampas fox
nodes.desc: A small canid of open country that eats cavies, hares and reptiles.

nodes.name: Turkey vulture
nodes.desc: A soaring scavenger that finds carrion by smell and feeds on dead animals along the coast.

nodes.name: South American sea lion
nodes.desc: The Islas de Torres hold the region's largest colony. Eats fish and squid and sometimes fur seals.

nodes.name: Orca
nodes.desc: A top marine predator that visits these waters and hunts seals and sea lions.
